global_caption: The video contains 7 shots. It is a multi-shot tutorial-style video in a realistic cool tone, set in a scorching desert fully frozen over. Wind-eroded ice dunes and frozen sand seas form a unified and subdued background. The overall color palette is dominated by blue-gray cool tones, with lighting based on overcast diffused cold light and faint reflections from icy surfaces.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in, using a wide shot at eye-level slightly low angle. Foreground features layered ice crust carved by wind; background shows undulating frozen dunes under a gray-white sky. The subject is a giant ice-scaled dragon standing beside a wind-eroded ice dune, with an ice crystal seven-string zither positioned in front. Lighting is cold and even, with slight glint along scale edges. Then it lifts the forepaw to support the zither while hind limbs provide firm balance, demonstrating the standard starting position. The camera slowly pushes in with a slight downward tilt, clearly establishing that the tutorial begins with overall posture.
shot2: Shot 2 cuts hard from the previous shot, using a close-up at eye-level. Depth of field is shallow, blurring the frozen dunes in the background. Focus centers on the left forepaw’s contact point with the zither body. The ice crystal support points and metal latches at the bottom form a stable triangular composition. The dragon slowly demonstrates how the left forepaw conforms to the side edge of the zither and secures the pressure point—claw tips not pressing strings, palm stabilizing weight.
shot3: Shot 3 cuts hard from the previous shot, using an extreme close-up at eye-level slightly upward angle. The frame includes only the forepaw’s thumb, string one, and part of the zither surface. Foreground has slightly blurred ice flake edges; background is darkened and out of focus to ensure visual emphasis remains on the thumb placement. Cold light sweeps across the string surface, creating a narrow highlight. The dragon slowly lowers the thumb from a hovering position, aligning it with the outermost string one—first demonstrating hover preparation, then light touch for positioning, finally stabilizing. A subtle ice shard collision The camera makes a minimal push-in and stops precisely at contact, locking the string-one correspondence.
shot4: Shot 4 connects via hard cut to the previous shot, using an extreme close-up at eye-level. Strings are arranged vertically across the frame, with index and middle fingers occupying central and right portions. Shallow depth of field separates string two and three spatially. The dragon first moves the index finger to string two and pauses briefly, then smoothly places the middle finger on string three. The two finger positions are not dropped simultaneously but demonstrated sequentially, emphasizing correspondence and preparatory posture. The camera performs a very short slide along the string direction, helping viewers distinguish the spatial order between string two and three.
shot5: Shot 5 transitions from the previous shot with a soft fade, using an extreme close-up overhead shot. The lens looks directly down at the zither surface and resonance plate, resembling a workbench perspective. The zither outline forms a natural frame around the image. The ring finger pressure point is centered visually. Ice surface reflections are more prominent but remain calm and consistent. The dragon slowly lowers the ring finger from a raised position to press the resonance plate, demonstrating depth and contact angle. Upon pressing, the plate shows slight deformation and minor changes in reflection, accompanied by a sharper ice shard adhesion The camera remains nearly locked, making only a minimal pitch adjustment upon completion, ensuring tutorial information is clearly readable.
shot6: Shot 6 cuts hard from the previous shot, using a medium shot at eye-level. Foreground shows partial zither stand structure; midground fully displays the forepaw and half the zither body; background reintroduces wind-eroded ice dunes as spatial reference. The dragon begins a combined pluck sequence from strings one to three: thumb hooks string one, index finger plucks string two, followed immediately by middle finger pulling string three. The motion evolves from isolated to fluid, with joint flexion, string rebound, and fine ice particles vibrating in sequence. Audibly, the three string contacts progress from sparse to dense, naturally building upon earlier single-finger instruction. The camera performs a slight follow-track along the subject’s right side with a gentle push-in, enhancing continuity without compromising tutorial clarity.
shot7: Shot 7 transitions from the previous shot with a slow pull-out fade, using a wide shot at eye-level slightly high angle. The dragon, ice crystal zither, wind-eroded ice dunes, and frozen sand sea are re-integrated into a unified frame. Foreground features ice patterns carved by cold wind. Subject is slightly left of center axis. Focus gradually shifts from the post-action forepaw back to overall posture. After completing the combined plucking, the dragon smoothly returns the forepaw to the standard starting position. The zither body becomes still, and cold light on the ice scales stabilizes. The camera slowly pulls back and rises slightly, concluding the entire tutorial with a standardized, clear, and reproducible ending pose.
